claim.quote: We report the detection of polarized anisotropy in the Cosmic Microwave Background radiation with the Degree Angular Scale Interferometer (DASI), located at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole research station.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal publication date was not read from a fetched source.

key_value_text.quote: the level found for the E-mode polarization is 0.80 (0.56 -- 1.10), where the predicted level given previous temperature data is 0.9 -- 1.1. At 95% confidence, an upper limit of 0.59 is set to the level of B-mode polarization
key_value_text.value: E-mode polarization level 0.80 (0.56-1.10) relative to the prediction; B-mode upper limit 0.59 at 95%; TE correlation detected at 95% confidence

name: Detection of Polarization in the Cosmic Microwave Background using DASI

official_url.quote: Detection of Polarization in the Cosmic Microwave Background using DASI

significance.quote: Specifically, E-mode polarization is detected at high confidence (4.9 sigma).

summary.plain: DASI, an interferometer at the South Pole, made the first detection of the polarization of the Big Bang afterglow. The pattern matched what theory predicts, supporting the standard picture of how structure began.
summary.technical: DASI 2001-2002 winter observations of two 3.4-degree fields: E-mode polarization detected at 4.9 sigma, TE correlation at 95% confidence, B-mode upper limit; consistent with adiabatic scalar perturbations.

title: Detection of Polarization in the Cosmic Microwave Background using DASI
why_it_matters: The three-year paper says it extends "the data from which the first detection of polarization of the cosmic microwave background radiation was reported".
